title: Galactic foregrounds & CMB delensing
summary: Finding a faint signal behind our Galaxy.

sections.Scientific question: How do residual Galactic foregrounds affect reconstructed CMB lensing and the removal of lensing-induced B modes?
sections.Why it matters: The search for primordial gravitational waves requires separating an extremely faint cosmological signal from brighter emission and lensing effects.
sections.My contribution: Developing simulation and analysis workflows to study foreground residuals, lensing reconstruction, and their propagation into parameter inference.
sections.Methods & tools: Python, CMB simulations, component separation, quadratic lensing estimators, and likelihood-based inference.
sections.Results & evidence: Quantitative results and publication details will be added alongside the corresponding figures and verified references.
sections.Transferable skills: Signal extraction, uncertainty propagation, reproducible simulations, and statistical validation.

title: Tomographic delensing with LSST × SO
summary: Using the galaxy distribution to understand CMB lensing.

sections.Scientific question: How can galaxy surveys split into redshift slices improve CMB delensing?
sections.Why it matters: Different observations contain complementary information about the matter that bends CMB light. Combining them can improve the recovery of a primordial signal.
sections.My contribution: Developing a tomographic delensing workflow using LSST galaxy tracers and Simons Observatory CMB observations.
sections.Methods & tools: Cross-correlations, tomographic galaxy bins, tracer weighting, simulations, and statistical inference.
sections.Results & evidence: Results and supporting figures are pending addition to this portfolio.
sections.Limitations & next steps: Assess sensitivity to photometric redshift uncertainty and galaxy bias modeling.

title: Point-spread function modeling
summary: Understanding how an instrument shapes the light we measure.

sections.Scientific question: How can point-spread function models support reliable measurements of astronomical sources?
sections.Why it matters: The response of an imaging system changes the appearance of a source and affects the accuracy of extracted measurements.
sections.My contribution: Scientific computing work on PSF modeling and astronomical image analysis.
sections.Methods & tools: Image processing, numerical modeling, fitting, and residual analysis.
sections.Results & evidence: Add the verified paper record and residual-comparison figures here.

title: 2D dynamo simulation
summary: Exploring magnetic-field evolution through numerical models.

sections.Scientific question: How can a two-dimensional dynamo model help investigate magnetic-field evolution and tachocline confinement?
sections.Why it matters: Numerical experiments make it possible to explore the interaction of flows and magnetic fields over time.
sections.My contribution: Developing a simulation project with an object-oriented C++ implementation, Python bindings, and an interactive visualization interface.
sections.Methods & tools: C++, Python, numerical methods, and simulation visualization.
sections.Results & evidence: Implementation and validation status will be documented with the project repository.
sections.Limitations & next steps: Add benchmark comparisons, input descriptions, and simulation animations.

title: Customer Retention Decision Analytics
summary: Turning churn risk into better retention decisions.

sections.Problem & intended user: Help an analytics team understand customer churn and evaluate retention interventions.
sections.Data & workflow: A planned workflow connects SQL analysis with feature exploration, PCA, churn modeling, SHAP explanations, and A/B testing.
sections.Design decisions: Separate prediction from intervention evaluation: a high churn score alone does not establish that an intervention will work.
sections.Evaluation approach: Use held-out discrimination and calibration checks, segment-level error analysis, and experiment uncertainty estimates.
sections.Results & evidence: No verified benchmark results are published here yet.
sections.Limitations & next steps: Document the dataset, complete reproducible evaluation, and publish decision-oriented findings.

title: PayWatch
summary: From transaction streams to auditable fraud signals.

sections.Problem & intended user: Help a fraud-monitoring team prioritize suspicious transactions and inspect scoring decisions.
sections.Data & workflow: The planned pipeline combines Kafka ingestion, an LSTM autoencoder, XGBoost scoring, ONNX Runtime, FastAPI, and PostgreSQL logging.
sections.Design decisions: Evaluate a two-stage scoring design to balance computational cost with the risk of missing fraudulent events during anomaly triage.
sections.Evaluation approach: Measure fraud recall, precision, false negatives at the triage stage, end-to-end latency, and behavior under delayed or duplicate events.
sections.Results & evidence: Latency and filtering targets are not reported as achieved results. Verified measurements are pending.
sections.Limitations & next steps: Complete end-to-end validation, establish baselines, and document drift monitoring and failure recovery.

title: DisasterLens
summary: Making image classification reproducible from training to deployment.

sections.Problem & intended user: Explore disaster image classification with a reproducible machine-learning workflow and an interactive demonstration.
sections.Data & workflow: AIDERv2 imagery, ResNet50 in PyTorch, preprocessing, augmentation, class-imbalance handling, and a planned interactive application.
sections.Design decisions: Treat evaluation and deployment checks as part of the model lifecycle. Keep training, inference, and application responsibilities separate.
sections.Evaluation approach: Use independent data splits, per-class precision and recall, confusion matrices, and failure-case inspection.
sections.Results & evidence: Model results and CI/CD execution evidence will be added after validation.
sections.Limitations & next steps: Document dataset limitations, verify automated tests, and publish a reproducible model and demo.
